The poem was enclosed in the sheet containing this letter, which was sealed with red wax
and addressed to Il Signor Williams (who was living in the same small building). As Michael
O’Neill notes, ‘there is a striking difference between the way the poem is written (beauti-
fully) and the way the letter to Williams is written (very “distrait,” possibly deliberately so)’
(MYRS viii p. xxi). Both poem and letter were in Jane Williams’s possession after the death
of Edward and S.; thereafter they were acquired by Trelawny, and passed on his death in
1881 to his daughter Laetitia (Mrs Charles F. Call), who presented them to Edinburgh Uni-
versity Library in 1907 (where they are shelfmarked ‘Dc. 1.100/4’). S.’s reference in the letter
to the portfolio of a friend suggests the distancing device of the draft prefaces to Epipsychid-
